headline: Kauno's first European home night, with Brann the favourites
summary: Kauno Žalgiris host their first home match in a European league phase on Thursday, and the market still makes Brann clear favourites. A 0-4 defeat at Brighton on matchday one, with just 0.04 expected goals created, explains the gap in level. Brann lost 1-3 at Vålerenga on Sunday but made 2.93 expected goals, and across 10 bookmakers they are 56.1% to win in Kaunas, with Kauno's head start in goals moving from 0.67 to 0.78. Kauno won 1-0 at Sūduva on Monday. Over 2.75 goals is priced at 51.2%.
read: Brann are clear favourites in Kaunas at 56.1%, rated about 0.8 goals the better side and strengthened in recent days, on the back of a Conference League opening win against a Kauno Žalgiris side that managed 0.04 xG in a 0-4 defeat at Brighton. The goals line sits at 2.75 with over at 51.2%, matching a Brann team averaging 2.14 xG for and 1.50 against over its last five.

facts.fact: Brann are 56.1% to win in Kaunas, more than two and a half times Kauno Žalgiris' 21.2%.
facts.meaning: The market sees a clear away favourite, with the draw at 22.7% only marginally ahead of the home side.

facts.fact: Kauno Žalgiris created just 0.04 xG in their 0-4 defeat at Brighton on matchday one, conceding 4.02.
facts.meaning: Against elite opposition they barely produced a chance, which is the backdrop to the market making them big underdogs here.

facts.fact: Brann lost 1-3 at Vålerenga on Sunday despite posting 2.93 xG, their second straight Eliteserien defeat.
facts.meaning: They are creating plenty but shipping goals — a profile that explains both the away favouritism and the goals line.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line has moved from Kauno +0.67 to +0.78 in Brann's favour in recent days.
facts.meaning: Brann are now rated about 0.8 goals the better side, with the main line sitting at Kauno +0.75.

facts.fact: Over 2.75 goals is priced at 51.2%, with the market's total-goals line up at 2.79.
facts.meaning: More likely than not, the market expects this to be a three-goal game or better.

facts.fact: Kauno Žalgiris won 1-0 away at Sūduva on Monday with a goal in the third minute of stoppage time.
facts.meaning: They arrive on a high and are closing in on the Lithuanian title, but with only three days between matches.

facts.fact: Kauno Žalgiris are playing their first-ever home match in the Conference League league phase, at the Darius and Girėnas Stadium.
facts.meaning: It is the biggest European home night in the club's history — a crowd and occasion factor the price already contains.

facts.fact: Kauno Žalgiris are 36th of 36 in the Conference League table after matchday one, with 0 points and a goal difference of -4; Brann are 12th on 3 points.
facts.meaning: The table already shows the gap: one side won its opener, the other was heavily beaten.

sources.fact: Kauno Žalgiris are playing their first-ever home match in the UEFA Conference League league phase against Brann at the Darius and Girėnas Stadium.
Kauno Žalgiris coach Ž. Sopićius said his team are proud and happy to play in a European competition and will give everything to win points against Brann.
Kauno Žalgiris beat Sūduva 1-0 away in the Toplyga on Monday with a goal in the third minute of stoppage time, moving close to their second league title.
Lithuanian media report that Kauno Žalgiris are closing in on a perfect Toplyga season after a 15-goal matchday 33.
Kauno Žalgiris lost 4-0 to Brighton on Conference League matchday one, with Georginio Rutter scoring twice.
Brann started their European season with an unexpectedly hard-fought win before travelling to Kaunas, according to Lithuanian media.
Brann are a century-old Norwegian club from Bergen whose history runs from the second division to the Conference League, as previewed before the match.
